questions.stem: Which is the correct statement about Bruch's membrane?

options.label: A
options.text: Basal lamina of the Iris

options.label: B
options.text: This is the layer of large vessels (Haller's layer).

options.label: C
options.text: This lines the layer of choriocapillaris

options.label: D
options.text: It is a thin membrane of condensed collagen fibers, melanocytes, and fibroblasts.

questions.answerText: This lines the layer of choriocapillaris
questions.solutionHtml:
This lines the layer of choriocapillaris
  • Basal lamina of choroid . It is also called Bruch's membrane and lines the layer of choriocapillaris. It lies in approximation with the pigment epithelium of the retina.

Choroid Anatomy

  • CHOROID: Choroid is the posterior-most part of the vascular coat of the eyeball.
  • It extends from the optic disc to the ora serrata.
  • Its inner surface is smooth and brown and lies in contact with the pigment epithelium of the retina.
  • The outer surface is rough and lies in contact with the sclera.


Comprehensive Ophthalmology by A K Khurana, 7th EditionPage No. 153

options.label: A

options.label: B

options.label: C
options.text: A- 1-iii, B- 3-i, C-2-ii

options.label: D
options.text: A- 2-ii, B- 1-i, C-3-iii

questions.solutionHtml:
A-> 3->iii, B-> 1->ii, C-2->ii
  • The ciliary muscle occupies most of the outer part of the ciliary body. In the cut section, it is triangular in shape.
  • It is a non-striated muscle having three parts:

(i) the longitudinal or meridional fibers which help in aqueous outflow;

(ii) the circular fibers which help in accommodation; and

(iii) the radial or oblique fibers act the same way as the longitudinal fibers.



Comprehensive Ophthalmology by A K Khurana, 7th EditionPage No. 133

questions.stemHtml: In the Ciliary zone of the iris, a series of radial streaks are present due to which of the following?

options.label: A
options.text: Underlying radial blood vessels and crypts are depressions where the superficial layer of the iris is missing.

options.label: B
options.text: Underlying longitudinal blood vessels and crypts are depressions where the superficial layer of the iris is denser.

options.label: C
options.text: Underlying radial blood vessels and crypts are depressions where the superficial layer of the iris is denser.

options.label: D
options.text: Underlying loose connective tissue and crypts are depressions where the superficial layer of the iris is missing.

questions.answerText: Underlying radial blood vessels and crypts are depressions where the superficial layer of the iris is missing.
questions.solutionHtml:
Underlying radial blood vessels and crypts are depressions where the superficial layer of the iris is missing.
  • Ciliary zone - It presents a series of radial streaks due to underlying radial blood vessels and crypts, depressions where a superficial layer of the iris is missing. Crypts are arranged in two rows —the peripheral present near the iris root and the central present near the collarette.

ANATOMY OF IRIS-

  • IRIS
  • Iris is the anterior-most part of the uveal tract. It is a thin circular disc corresponding to the diaphragm of a camera.
  • In its center is an aperture of about 4 mm diameter called a pupil, which regulates the amount of light reaching the retina. At the periphery, the iris is attached to the middle of the anterior surface of the ciliary body. It divides the space between the cornea and lens into anterior and posterior chambers.



Comprehensive Ophthalmology by A K Khurana, 7th EditionPage No. 133

questions.stemHtml: Find out the wrong statement regarding the IRIS.

options.label: A
options.text: Sphincter pupillae muscle works under the parasympathetic impulse to constrict the pupil, and the dilator pupillae muscle works under the sympathetic impulse to dilate the pupil

options.label: B
options.text: The sphincter pupillae retain their function even if severed radially because of its unique distribution of fibres.

options.label: C
options.text: Iris nerves are usually myelinated; however, Schwann cells find all nerves enclosed.

options.label: D
options.text: Pigment dispersion syndrome is a bilateral condition characterized by the liberation of pigment granules from the iris pigment epithelium.

questions.answerText: Iris nerves are usually myelinated; however, Schwann cells find all nerves enclosed.
questions.solutionHtml:
Iris nerves are usually myelinated; however, Schwann cells find all nerves enclosed.
  • The sphincter pupillae muscle forms a one-millimeter broad circular band in the pupillary part of the iris. It is supplied by parasympathetic fibres through the third nerve.
  • It constricts the pupil. The dilator pupillae muscle lies in the posterior part of the stroma of the ciliary zone of the iris.

questions.stem: A 40 year female patient presented with pulsatile exophthalmos along with proptosis, chemosis, bruit, and progressive dimness of vision. On examination, it shows orbital edema, extraocular muscles are enlarged and ruptured ICH and raised intracranial pressure. Which blood vessels show enlargement in CT?

options.label: A
options.text: Superior Ophthalmic Vein

options.label: B
options.text: Inferior ophthalmic vein

options.label: C
options.text: Minor arterial circle

options.label: D
options.text: Major arterial circle

questions.solutionHtml:
Superior Ophthalmic Vein
  • Carotico-cavernous fistula -> raised episcleral venous pressure due to A-V fistula, e., ICA to cavernous sinus -> enlargement of the superior ophthalmic vein.
  • CAROTID-CAVERNOUS FISTULA
  • Carotid-cavernous fistula is an acquired abnormal communication between the carotid arterial system and the venous cavernous sinus.
  • Clinical types
  • There are two types of carotid-cavernous fistula:
  • High-flow fistula is secondary to trauma or iatrogenic and presents acutely with pain and proptosis (often pulsatile exophthalmos). Chemosis, congestion, bruit, ophthalmoplegia (nerve palsies), headache, and objective pulsatile tinnitus.
  • The classical triad of presentation is proptosis, chemosis, and bruit.
  • It presents within days or weeks following trauma.
  • Low-flow fistula: These develop spontaneously in elderly women, during pregnancy, or in those with hyperplastic tissue. These typically present slowly with less pronounced symptoms.


Comprehensive Ophthalmology by A K Khurana, 4th Edition, Page No. 381
